prompt:
Paint ONE place into this tile of a painted grand-strategy map. The input is the finished map around the place, seen straight down; the place stands at the exact CENTRE of the image.

The place: Trường Vân Thành, city. Paint it as a walled city: a rectangular wall with gate towers, dense grey-tile roofs inside, a central tower or palace, a market square, suburbs along the roads outside the walls.
How it looks: A walled harbour city at the edge of the desert, where a river reaches the sea under the snow mountains. A long roofed caravan gallery runs straight through the city from the land gate to the docks, so goods pass from camel to ship without seeing the sun. On cloudy days a faint shimmer of a ward formation hangs over the walls, and long clouds lie on the peaks behind.
Art brief: A small painted miniature of a rectangular walled harbour city of grey-tile roofs at a river mouth on the sea, with desert sand on its landward side. Straight through its middle runs a long continuous roofed caravan gallery from the land gate to the docks, the signature element. A gate tower of three roofs is the tallest outline; a faint translucent shimmer of a ward dome over the walls. Ships at the quays. Warm golden-hour light from the top left. No text, no people larger than specks, nothing outside the city.

Rules:
- Paint the place as a small, finely detailed miniature, as if a model-maker had built it into this painted relief: seen from above at a gentle angle so roofs, walls and towers read clearly, its base sitting naturally on the terrain that is there (follow the slopes, the shore, the river).
- Keep it centred and compact: the whole place fits inside a circle about 22 % of the image width across the centre. Short roads or paths may lead out of it.
- Match the map exactly: the same golden-hour light from the TOP LEFT with soft shadows to the bottom right, the same painterly style, colours and level of detail as the surrounding terrain; the building scale fits the trees and hills around it.
- Leave everything outside that central circle exactly as it is in the input.
- Never: text, labels, banners with writing, flags with symbols, people larger than specks, a frame, a vignette, clouds over the place.
